$comment: Authorities that must NEVER appear in any shipped artifact.
Six external models reviewed this concept and produced these. Each was
checked against primary sources and found false, fabricated, or
misattributed. Two of the case citations exist in no legal database at all.
This file is the fixture behind a CI gate. Citing invented authority in a
legal-domain product, in front of judges, is the single most damaging
honesty failure available to this project, so the prohibition is mechanical
The scanner deliberately excludes this file and its test from its own sweep.
A non-vacuity test plants a blacklisted string in a temporary tracked file
and asserts detection, so the exclusion cannot render the guard inert.

It does not hold that curtailment is an individualized administrative judgment. Anchor on 23 CCR 875(b), Stanford Vina Ranch (2020) and California Water Curtailment Cases (2022) instead.

allowlist_comment: Authorities that MAY appear in a drafted order. Everything else is stripped.
An allowlist, not a denylist, and the direction matters. A denylist stops
the fabrications you already know about; six external models reviewing this
concept invented case law nobody had seen before, including two cases that
exist in NO database. You cannot blacklist a citation nobody has invented
Every entry was verified against a primary source. Adding one without doing
that defeats the whole mechanism, so the pattern field is deliberately
narrow: it matches the citation as it must be written, not loosely.
Every numeric pattern carries a RIGHT-HAND BOUNDARY. Without one, 'Water Code
1846' matched the prefix of the fabricated 'Water Code 18460' and, combined
with an overlap-based allow test, waved the invention through. Case entries
carry their reporter cites so a FULLY cited verified authority survives.
